arguments.command:
python3 << 'EOF'
import math

# Data from the table (in millions of dollars)
# Month | Bonds | Bills and certificates of indebtedness
data = [
    ("1941-December", 40000, 2002),
    ("1942-January", 42078, 2101),
    ("1942-February", 44305, 2002),
    ("1942-March", 44847, 1652),
    ("1942-April", 45360, 3460),
    ("1942-May", 48157, 3764),
    ("1942-June", 48776, 5604),
    ("1942-July", 51765, 6759),
    ("1942-August", 53680, 8873),
    ("1942-September", 54413, 10829),
    ("1942-October", 57285, 11336),
    ("1942-November", 57931, 12882),
    ("1942-December", 64868, 17161),
]

# Extract values
bonds = [d[1] for d in data]
bills = [d[2] for d in data]

n = len(bonds)
print(f"Number of data points: {n}")
print(f"Bonds: {bonds}")
print(f"Bills: {bills}")

# Calculate means
mean_bonds = sum(bonds) / n
mean_bills = sum(bills) / n
print(f"\nMean Bonds: {mean_bonds}")
print(f"Mean Bills: {mean_bills}")

# Calculate Pearson correlation coefficient
# r = Σ[(xi - x̄)(yi - ȳ)] / √[Σ(xi - x̄)² * Σ(yi - ȳ)²]

numerator = sum((bonds[i] - mean_bonds) * (bills[i] - mean_bills) for i in range(n))
sum_sq_bonds = sum((bonds[i] - mean_bonds) ** 2 for i in range(n))
sum_sq_bills = sum((bills[i] - mean_bills) ** 2 for i in range(n))

denominator = math.sqrt(sum_sq_bonds * sum_sq_bills)

r = numerator / denominator

print(f"\nNumerator: {numerator}")
print(f"Denominator: {denominator}")
print(f"\nPearson correlation coefficient: {r}")
print(f"Rounded to 3 decimal places: {round(r, 3)}")
EOF
